newsitem.title: INDIA: India SBI foreign branches net up 55 pct.
newsitem.headline: India SBI foreign branches net up 55 pct.

text.p: India's largest commercial bank, the state-run State Bank of India (SBI), said on Thursday its network of 52 foreign branches had earned a net profit of 1.44 billion rupees during fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).

"The bank's foreign offices improved their performance during the year and earned a net profit of 1.4 billion rupees, recording a net increase of 55 percent over the previous year," SBI said in a statement.
In the merchant banking segment, SBI said it had arranged 20 sydnicated transactions totalling $1.46 billion during the year.
It also extended short-term foreign currency loans amounting to over one billion dollars to various Indian firms and over $225 million in medium-term loans during the same period.
